title: Plautus ex umbria Sarsinas Romae moritur anno ab urbe condita millessimo
shelf_note: No tradition or collection assigned; a 15th-c. humanist manuscript of Plautus (Amphitruo) with a Latin Batrachomyomachia — a classical text, outside the core esoteric shelves but a legitimate primary source.
structure_note: Composite manuscript: pp. 29 and 51 are Plautus' Amphitruo (51 = its explicit, 'Finit Amphitrio comoedia'), p. 74 is Marsuppini's Latin Batrachomyomachia. The title covers only the Plautus part. 113 of 114 pages have OCR and 89 have translations. Nothing in the counts suggests a splice.

title: [Fragmenta sive libri manualis de universis festivitatibus et dominicos et singulis diebus ecclesiae Mediolanensis, cum psalterio canticis et hymnis]
shelf_note: No tradition assigned; a 14th-c. Ambrosian (Milanese) liturgical manuscript with neumes — a liturgical primary source.
structure_note: Each of the 4 'pages' is a microfilm strip of several openings: p. 2 has six openings at 221 px tall, p. 4 six at 225 px, p. 3 two at 664 px. A reader cannot read pp. 2 and 4 at all, and each record transcribes only a selection. The page unit is wrong (I5/I7-like), not one leaf per record.

title: Historiarum Florentinarum libri XII
shelf_note: Bruni's History of the Florentine People (Strasbourg: Zetzner, 1610), from the John Adams/BPL collection; a humanist historical source.
structure_note: Image and text are out of step, and the gap grows through the book: image 82 shows printed p. 67 but its text is p. 68; image 162 shows p. 143 but its text is p. 148; image 243 shows p. 222 but its text is p. 229. This is a systematic text/image misalignment across the book, not a misread numeral.

title: Carmen elegia gratulatoria in honorem et gratiam Martini Fabricii zuellichiensis…
shelf_note: No tradition assigned; a 1583 Frankfurt (Oder) academic occasional poem bound in a Sammelband. A minor but genuine primary source.
structure_note: Pp. 9 and 13 are a later (18th/19th-c.) handwritten inventory of a Sammelband of occasional prints (items 89–173, dated 1588–1610). They are not the 1583 elegy the title names. The printed poem (sig. A2) begins only around p. 19, and its addressee is a 'docte Sabine', so it may be another piece in the volume. The 29-page record looks like the bound volume's manuscript index plus one print. Pages translated (19) are fewer than pages with OCR (29).
